chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad and Ahmad, the sons of al-Hasan, from their father from Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked

about a man who bequeathed wealth for the Hajj, but it was not enough to perform Hajj from his homeland. He said, 'He is given [the funds] in the place where it is sufficient to perform Hajj on his behalf.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a bequest for Hajj is insufficient to cover the cost of pilgrimage from one's home country?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of proportional fulfillment for Hajj bequests, ensuring the specific intent of the testator is honored even if resources are limited. It reflects the Shia juristic approach of prioritizing the actualization of the bequest's purpose over rigid adherence to the ideal of a full pilgrimage from the place of origin, thereby preventing the funds from being idle or misallocated.
